text_en:
The final of {event} is over. {team} lost to {opponent}, {final_score}.

You take off your headset. A moment ago you were still planning the next round, but there will be no next round tonight. Your opponents come over to shake hands, gold confetti settling on their shoulders. You watch them walk toward the trophy. The arena is deafening, and none of this cheering belongs to you.

Back in the lounge, nobody speaks for a while. The coach hands you some water. 'Don't put every mistake on yourself tonight. When we've caught our breath, we'll look at it together.'

{player}, second place matters. You do not have to pretend to be satisfied with it already. Be upset tonight. When you turn the game on again, work out how to get back here.

choices.continue: Pack up and leave with your teammates

text_en:
New stories about life and competing are ready. You can start experiencing them now, or keep this career at its existing pace.
Past matches will not be recalculated, and missed choices will not be replayed.

choices.no: Keep this save as it is

text_en:
She does not quite understand trades and retakes, but remembers when your practice finishes. You share a hot meal outside a convenience store. After hearing about the match, she asks whether you ate properly today, not how badly you lost.
You like the quiet. She has a job and worries of her own; cheering for you is not her entire life. You agree to say when you are busy rather than leave each other guessing.

choices.ok: Take your time getting to know each other

text_en:
She always knows what to say on camera. Off stream, she does not always feel like talking. You realise she needs a break from other people's attention just as much as you do.
You talk about content, practice and keeping some life to yourselves. She is in no hurry to announce the relationship. 'Some happy things can stay between two people for a while.'
You promise to ask her first when something happens, instead of treating the comments as an answer.

choices.ok: Make time for each other off camera

text_en:
Shen Yuning's schedule is as crowded as your tournament calendar. Your first date is rearranged three times and ends up being a hot drink at an airport before dawn. She takes off her cap and smiles. 'No interview today. Let's talk about something that doesn't matter quite so much.'
You both know what attention costs, and neither wants a partner who exists only in the margins of a career. Meetings are rare, but you make proper time for them.
Understanding brought you together. You will have to keep practising it.

romance_pace.title_en: The gaps in the practice schedule
text_en:
Several tournaments have passed since you started dating. During this break, you realise you have become used to checking her messages as soon as you wake up. Last night's conversation ran late. This morning, the alarm has rung twice and you are still in bed.
Your coach sends the date practice resumes. You forward it to her. 'Then what are we doing these next few days?' she asks. You look at the calendar. It is time to be clear about both seeing her and practising.

choices.heat: Enjoy being in love (extra positive and negative form swings until the next Major ends)
choices.focus: Keep practice and rest on schedule

marriage.title_en: A future without the time difference
text_en:
Six months into the relationship, {partner} brings up marriage seriously for the first time. She wants a life that does not revolve around counting the days until you meet again. She hopes you will stop spending long stretches abroad for tournaments.
This is more than an offhand complaint. You also know that competing still belongs in your future.
Her wish does not automatically make you wrong, and your dream cannot answer for her. Tonight you need to make a real decision.

choices.stay: Stay and consider ending your playing career
choices.abroad: Keep competing abroad and accept the breakup
choices.talk: Talk it through (50% chance of reaching an agreement)

confirm_love.title_en: Retirement, not a few days off
text_en:
You understand that retiring cannot guarantee a relationship. One promise cannot keep it together on its own.
Your results and honours will remain recorded. Are you sure you accept this future?

choices.back: I'm not ready. Let's talk again

stable.title_en: A future with room for both of you
text_en:
One conversation has not solved everything. But you have stopped treating each other's wishes as a threat. {partner} agrees to keep facing the distance, and you make plans for time together that you can actually keep.
'I'll miss you. I don't want you blaming me for everything you wish you'd done, either.'
When the next controversy comes, there is somewhere you can speak without first proving yourself.

You finish the conversation and admit that the lives you want do not fit together right now. No doors slam. Nobody wins the argument. The chat simply grows quieter.
You put your ticket away and return to the practice room on time the next day. Choosing competition still hurts. After the hurt, you still know where you want to go.

choices.ok: Remember the relationship, then carry on

press.title_en: The comments won't play your next round

choices.retire: Consider retirement and a different life

text_en: You can stop taking on this pressure. Retiring also means this playing career really ends here. Nobody knows exactly what will come next.

choices.yes: Retire and try a different life
choices.back: I still want to play another match

text_en:
You do not reply to every comment. After practice, a teammate marks a piece of teamwork on the timeline. 'We fix this together. It isn't just on you.'
The noise outside will not stop immediately. You turn your attention from proving you deserve your place to working out how to play the next round.

You close social media and leave a page of review notes open. The coach does not promise a win next time. Instead, he breaks the problems into things you can practise today.
You do not need to pretend there is no pressure. You need to complete a useful practice session with it still there.

This is not one bad tournament. You have won only {wins} of the last {series_count} series, and several events in a row ended without a single victory.
{allies} approach you privately. They want to ask the club to replace {target}.
They call it the first step of a rebuild. {target} says the problems have never belonged to just one person. Now they want your answer.

choices.neutral: Stay out of it; ask management to judge the matches

neutral_reply.title_en: You did not sign the list
text_en:
You ask for everyone's mistakes to go into the review, instead of making one name the answer. Some think you have refused to take a side. The targeted teammate finally exhales.
Management keeps the roster for now. The disagreement has not disappeared, but nobody can use your silence to claim the entire team agreed.

na_start.title_en: A gear bag beside the acceptance letter
text_en:
Your family sent you to North America to study. In the game, you have discovered a talent that makes a professional career seem possible.
This is the timed NA student challenge: you start with {na_bonus} extra attribute points. The first assessment lasts {na_first_year_days} days. Your personal benchmark is at least {na_min_maps} official maps with an average map Career Rating of {na_min_rating}.
Your family's support gives you room to try. It cannot do the work of living every possible life for you.

choices.pro: Leave your studies and focus on competing

lvg_invite.title_en: Lynn Vision: we want to hear your voice
text_en:
Dear {player},

We have watched your matches in North America, including how you approached the next match when things went badly. We are writing because of more than a good statistic. We noticed your willingness to learn and communicate in an unfamiliar environment.

Lynn Vision would like to invite you home to join our active roster in a suitable role. We cannot promise applause at every event. We can offer a clear practice plan, a full team around you, and a chance to treat competition as a long-term profession.

Coming home does not erase your year abroad. We want you to bring that experience into this team. Please think carefully about the people with whom you want to spend the next part of your career.

The Lynn Vision coaching and operations team

choices.no: Thank them, but stay on your current path

na_return.title_en: The return flight is not the end
text_en:
After reading the letter, going home is no longer something you avoid discussing. You have not won the agreed title or accepted a new professional offer. You do not have to wait until everything has failed to come home.
After confirming, you will restart with a self-created team at home. Your ability, items and history remain; the old club's money does not belong to you. The roster change waits for current tournaments to finish.
The second assessment starts on the day you actually return and rebuild, lasting {na_return_days} days. Either a recognised title or {na_min_maps} official maps averaging Career Rating {na_min_rating} will meet the requirement.

choices.ok: Return home, build a team and try again

dota_partner.title_en: She understands another kind of mistake
text_en:
Some time after coming home, you meet a woman who makes Dota content. It is a different game, but she understands nights spent regretting missed timings, blaming yourself too much and refusing to give up.
You start talking after your work is done. She is not a prize or another assessment. She is someone willing to face the results with you.

reunion.title_en: On the other side this time
text_en:
Your next opponent is your most recent former team: {old_team}. Familiar names have moved from your team list to the other side.
Someone asks how you feel before the match. What will you say?

choices.bold: Talk big: I won't hold anything back today
choices.respect: Respect the past; give everything on the server
choices.quiet: Decline the interview and let the match speak

love_home.text_en:
You stayed, and she kept her part of the promise. Married life is not bright every day. There are conversations, arguments, and meals shared after the arguments.
Later you begin streaming. Your wife often sits beside you for a few games. People ask what might have happened if you had kept competing. You sometimes wonder too, without using that imagined life to condemn the one you have.
You did not become the legend everyone expected. You have a home you keep wanting to return to.

love_stream.text_en:
You ended your playing career, but the relationship ended anyway. At first the stream from your rented room is quiet. You discuss demos with nobody answering and thank the occasional viewer who stays.
Then another FPS arrives. You shift the stream to it. Your professional experience helps you learn quickly; all those hours talking to an empty room have taught you how to speak. More people begin watching.
They still joke about your old choice. Sometimes you laugh along; sometimes you admit it hurt. One loss no longer settles your entire life. You have found a place on a different map.

press_stream.text_en:
Retirement does not instantly make you a famous streamer. You turn your professional experience into details ordinary viewers can understand, work on your content, and slowly gather people who want to listen.
Eventually the stream thrives. You sometimes recall the sound outside the booth after a match. Those mistakes have become part of how you understand players and viewers.
There is more than one path through life. You still love the stage without needing to stand on it to prove yourself.

press_other.text_en:
Streaming is harder than you expected. Keeping a schedule, finding topics and holding an audience all demand something different from good aim. After trying it for a while, you admit it is not the job you want for the long term.
You turn off the equipment, learn another skill and start a different career. When friends mention an old match, you can still describe the final round exactly.
The years of competing were not wasted. They do not have to be the only thing you can introduce yourself with.

study_fail.text_en:
A year has passed. You did not win the agreed title, and your studies slipped as they kept making room for matches. You believed effort would be enough to hold both together. There was less time than you thought.
Your family is still there to support you. You return to your courses and make new plans. One attempt does not have to remove every way forward.
This professional challenge ends here. It does not prove you have no talent. The next attempt will need a workable schedule as well as love for the game.

caster.title_en: Your turn to tell the match
caster.text_en:
Another year at home passes without a title. You admit you have not reached the place you once imagined. Yet whenever you commentate a match on stream, people stay to listen.
Your playing experience helps you explain decisions. Your way with words makes those moments accessible to more than insiders. You start with small broadcasts and gradually become a popular caster.
After your first major broadcast, she messages: 'You were really good just then.' You look toward the other side of the stage. You still belong to the world you love.

wish: {teammate} pushes the cake toward you. 'Thought you'd forgotten again. Thanks. Biggest slice is yours tonight.' The others start demanding that the birthday boy buy dinner. For once, the practice room talks about something other than matches.
{teammate} gives you a quiet, sincere thank-you. Before practice the next day, he leaves your usual drink beside your desk. 'I appreciated what you said yesterday.'
Your singing is out of tune, and the teammates laugh louder than the birthday boy. {teammate} records it but does not post it. 'This one stays in our group chat.'
train: {teammate} sees that you are practising and eventually replies, 'Okay. Don't stay up too late.' He still saves you a slice of cake in an unmarked box. You can tell he understands, and that he is a little disappointed.

Someone points out that the match is close. {teammate} waves it away. 'I know. He always takes it seriously.' Later he comes to the practice-room door and asks if you want food, without mentioning the birthday again.
The next day, someone jokes that the party was missing one terrible singer. {teammate} laughs, then says plainly, 'Next time, saying happy birthday won't ruin your practice, will it?'

texts_en: After several counter-strafes, the pulling sensation in your wrist does not fade as usual. You slow down. A movement you never had to think about now needs care.
Your mouse hand is still tight after practice. A teammate notices you shaking it out and quietly removes the extra session from the schedule.
You used to think a minor ache would disappear overnight. This morning, lifting a glass is uncomfortable. You decide to stop ignoring it.
Halfway through the review, you realise your shoulders have been tense for ages. Turning toward the screen is stiff. Last night's extra practice has caught up with you.
Travel ran straight into practice, and your shoulders never relaxed. After watching you adjust your seat several times, the coach pauses the demo and asks whether you should be practising today.
You once recovered from late matches with a night's sleep. Now the stiffness follows you into tomorrow. Recovery needs a place on the schedule too.
A series of wide flicks makes the ache in your elbow obvious. You stop the last training set and admit your movements are less steady today.
The mousepad and movements have not changed. Your arm is simply unwilling to keep repeating them forever. A teammate suggests skipping a set. This time you agree.
The practice numbers do not reveal where you hurt. When you stand and hold your arm for a moment, the coach drops his suggestion of another session.
Small pains when you click begin to disrupt your rhythm. Gripping the mouse harder will not fix it. Your touch will be less consistent for a while.
After practice, your fingers still curl as though holding the mouse. You slowly relax them and consider how many times you repeated that motion today.
The opponent has not become faster; your movement is half a beat late. Not every mistake comes from a lack of effort. Sometimes your body needs you to listen.
In the last rounds you keep shifting in your chair. The ache draws your attention away, and even a familiar clutch takes extra effort to focus on.
Your bags are packed, but bending down makes you stop. A teammate takes your gear bag without a joke and reminds you not to put recovery last.
The practice room is quiet except for your chair as you keep getting up. You stop pretending you recover like you did when you were younger and put breaks into the schedule.
You wake feeling as if you have not slept. You can see every timestamp in the review but struggle to remember any of it. Exhaustion is not simply a failure to try hard enough.
Even a win fails to excite you. Travel, practice and matches have run into one another. Today you notice how long it has been since you truly stopped.
You watch the same clip three times. The coach closes his notebook. 'That's enough today. Taking your career seriously doesn't always mean pushing through.'
The map is familiar, but keeping your eyes focused grows harder. You stop practice and spend a while looking at the light outside instead of the screen.
During the last set, you keep blinking. A teammate closes his game first and takes you to dinner, giving you a reason to rest without having to explain.
You always say one more demo before bed. Today you stop before saying it. Wanting to win more does not make screen time limitless.
The familiar discomfort returns. You no longer panic as you did the first time. You lay out the practice and recovery plans again. This will take patience.
The packed schedule brings back an ache that had eased. You do not blame your past self; you leave more room in the next few weeks.
A teammate asks how you feel. This time you do not answer, 'Fine.' Telling the truth does not automatically cost you your starting place. It may help you keep playing.

legend.title_en: A name left on the stage
legend.text_en:
You have said you are retiring. The records on the honours wall will not disappear: Major titles, tournament trophies and annual rankings give this career a weight of its own.
You no longer need another match to prove what you have already done. New names will arrive. Your page remains here.

veteran.text_en:
You look at the next tournament's schedule and decide not to put your name on the list. Several full seasons have passed since your first official appearance.
This goodbye does not have to mean slower reactions or follow a crushing loss. After a long journey, you want to spend the next stretch of time on another part of life.
A teammate asks if you will still play together. You smile and say yes, just without setting an alarm to catch the next match.

early_success.title_en: Taking your achievements down another road
early_success.text_en:
You decide to end your playing career. It has brought genuine achievements, recorded honours you worked to earn.
Some think it is too early; others understand. You do not pretend time has worn you out. You simply want to spend what comes next on something else.
Those results are still yours. Ending a journey does not require calling the whole of it a failure.

plain.text_en:
You tell the team you are retiring. There is no need to dress this up as the end of a decades-long campaign, or pretend you never seriously wanted to win.
The match records stay in your save. The rest of your life will be about more than their scores. You pack your gear and consider what you want to do next.
This time, the next step is not on the tournament calendar.

start.create.street.text_en: There is no sponsor wall in {team}'s first photo. You put the team name on the entry form and check who is free next week. Good ladder games are not yet team chemistry, and your balance cannot take careless spending. Sort out roles, read the invitations, and finish your first match. {player}, this is a career, not one evening's winning streak.

start.create.academy.text_en: You turn your old practice notebook to a blank page and write {team}. Earlier pages contain rehearsed plays and mistakes you still make. Now you must play your role and help decide how the team uses a limited budget. Before the first invitation arrives, get to know the four people beside you. A bigger stage must be earned, event by event.

start.create.prodigy.text_en: People remember {player}'s crosshair, but do not yet know {team}. Imagining the spotlight is tempting. The budget and teammates in front of you are more immediate. You can take another opening kill, but cannot make every trade for everyone. Turn your advantage into rounds the team can reproduce.

start.2024.donk.text_en: A young menace quietly arrives in Katowice. On this stage, you are the newcomer. Across from you, opponents laugh and talk, seemingly unconcerned by your presence. That is fine. You feel the same way.

start.2025.zywoo.text_en: France's ultimate weapon, Counter-Strike's chosen one. Last year's journey still had its difficulties. What ambitions lie behind that calm expression?

start.2026.niko.text_en: When NiKo first emerged, winning a Major seemed only a matter of time. Now, time itself appears to be the problem.

first.lan.text_en: Entering the player corridor at {event}, you hear the crowd through the walls. You know the sound of keyboards in the practice room; hearing {team} called on a stage like this is new. Connect your gear. Check the headset. However bright the lights, the first round still begins with the crosshair in front of you.

first.final.text_en: Only one fixture remains at {event}, and {team} is in it. Earlier wins brought you here without putting any extra rounds on the final's scoreboard. Teammates check the maps as you put your hand back on the mouse. Wanting to win is overwhelming. The next thing you do still needs to be specific.

title.major.text_en: The roar of the arena hits you. You jump up. All those days and nights of scrims have brought you here. Together you raise the trophy, lights shifting across it. Your opponents have left the stage. From now on, {short} champions belongs beside {team}'s name. Gold confetti lands on your face. You know this is not the end.

title.premier.text_en: This is no illusion or warmup. As the cameras turn toward you, nobody calls the result an accident. {team} have won {event}. You look at your teammates and find them looking back. This time, you are the ones on top.

title.t1.text_en: Someone calls your team's name in the corridor. Others are already discussing the next event, but you want a little more of tonight. {event} is over. {team} are champions. The trophy will cool in your hands; the memory will not.

title.t2.text_en: Bigger stages can wait. Tonight, the drinks are warm. When {team} close the score at {short}, your breathing finally slows. Win this one first. Tomorrow you can talk about the rest of the road.

title.cct.text_en: The match page finally lists {team} as champions of {event}. Someone counts points; someone else reviews the last clutch. You do not have to call this the peak of a career. It is a real step forward. Before leaving voice chat, you agree on the next practice.

title.default.a.text_en: You won. {team} now occupy the champions' line at {event}. Some sigh with relief; others have begun the review. You leave the score page open a little longer before moving on.

title.default.b.text_en: Someone pats your shoulder. Someone starts unplugging equipment. The trophy is still on the table, its metal cool. {team}, champions of {short}. You repeat it silently before believing it.

top20.eve.lock.text_en: Tomorrow, twenty names from this year will be read out. Your performances have all but secured your place. You no longer have to wonder whether you are among them. The question is how high.

top20.eve.edge.text_en: The annual ranking is almost here. You look through the year's reports: some excellent matches, others you could have played better. Your place must wait for the final selection. Close the notebook for tonight. A year is more than a ranking, but you still want to see it.

top20.eve.miss.text_en: Tomorrow they will read the names from twentieth upward. You know you are probably not among them. The road ahead remains, and you will keep walking it.
